title: permission sets: the body `packageId`'s remaining sites after #23259 — the install and registration door overrides a disagreeing value silently, and two consumer readers still fall back to it
body:
Filing gate: **(b) a declared key that a door silently overrides**, one family card for the remaining sites of the same key (one ruling, one key, three locations). `reach:` the package install and registration door (`ObjectQL.registerApp` → `registerItem`), measured in-process by the #23259 dev on a host kernel; the two consumer readers by reading. Source: the #23259 dev report (`os-dev-report` on #23259, out-of-scope findings 2 and 3), PR #23311. Reader who acts: triage, to grade and route; then the owning seat.

`Seam: spec:PermissionSetSchema.packageId → runtime:ObjectQL.registerApp / registerItem (no owner judge) | consumers: plugin-security declaredPackageIdOf, cli permission-set-name-collisions (read the body key when the binding is absent)`

Filed by `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · `os-justin` · session `session_01BRQ9Mp1yH7R1az6MaUM18H`, at the review of PR #23311. ⛔ Not a claim.

## The ruling this card inherits

#23259's seat ruling (claim `6149212588`, dispatch Zone 1): a permission set's body `packageId` must agree with its package binding, or the write is refused with a prescription; ADR-0086 D3 declares the key ("the owning package for a package-shipped set (absent ⇒ env-authored)"). PR #23311 applies it at the save and publish doors (and, after its patch round, the restore doors) and makes `declaredOwnerOf` read the binding only. This card carries the same ruling to the sites that PR does not reach.

## 1. The install and registration door overrides a disagreeing body key silently

- A package artifact whose permission set declares `packageId: 'com.probe.other'`, registered through `registerApp` from package `com.probe.pkg`, is registered under `com.probe.pkg` with no refusal and no warning (probe A1 in the #23259 report). `os validate` and `os build` say nothing either.
- No in-tree producer was measured (examples and HotCRM `0f84c9c`: no non-test permission set with a body `packageId`), so today it is a trap for a package author, or an AI, who copies a set from another package.

## 2. Two consumer readers still fall back to the body key

- `plugin-security` `packaged-permission-set-lock.ts`, `declaredPackageIdOf`: reads `_packageId ?? packageId` (tenant-authored items excluded).
- `cli` `permission-set-name-collisions.ts`: reads `manifestId ?? ps.packageId` (a single-package stack with no manifest id; a warning only).
- Both are dormant (no in-tree producer measured). Under the ruling the binding alone decides the owner, as `declaredOwnerOf` now does.

## Wanted

- Item 1: a package whose permission set's body `packageId` disagrees with the package is refused at the build door (`defineStack` / `os validate`) with the #23259 prescription, and the registration door does not override it silently. Where the check lives is the owning seat's measurement.
- Item 2: both readers read the binding only, each with a pin and a negative control.

Order: after PR #23311 lands (its prescription and judge are the ones to reuse).

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on this repo, closed included: `registerApp package artifact permission set packageId names another package silently registered override os validate` → 13 hits. #23259 (open) is the save and publish doors; #23233 (open) is the projection's dropped `_packageId`; #22689, #23074, #22189, #22024, #19577, #18202, #17516 and #16891 (closed) are other registration, validation and package-id questions. None is this.

Dedupe words: registerApp permission packageId mismatch; package artifact permission set packageId override; declaredPackageIdOf fallback; permission-set-name-collisions packageId.
